source.title: Exploring vocabulary alignment of neurons in Llama-3.2-1B

record.file_problem: none; the full post text is present
record.tranche_reason: The post measures vocabulary alignment of neuron output weights, but does not measure whether neurons have one main job, test explanations on held-out activations, or otherwise test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern closeness between MLP output weights and vocabulary embeddings. The post raises monosemanticity as a follow-up question but does not measure it. The vocabulary-alignment findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The post measures how closely Llama-3.2-1B MLP output weights align with vocabulary unembeddings (logit lens on weights). It does not audit neurons for one main job, score explanations, or test any version. It explicitly leaves monosemanticity as an open follow-up question.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author finds strong vocabulary alignment in a subset of neurons, especially in later layers. Whether this relates to monosemanticity or function is posed as an open question.
record.recipe_differences: The post projects MLP output weights into vocabulary space using dot products; it does not apply the original neuron-job audit or test explanation fidelity.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports stronger vocabulary alignment particularly in later blocks.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, layer-13 MLP output weights show a long-tailed distribution of maximum dot product with vocabulary unembeddings. Neurons with stronger alignment are concentrated in later blocks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A subset of MLP neurons, especially in later layers, write outputs closely aligned with specific vocabulary tokens or token clusters.

record.problems: The post does not quantify the share of aligned neurons or test whether vocabulary alignment correlates with monosemanticity. The layer-wise findings are described qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: The post lists top vocabulary matches for the first 20 neurons in layer 13, but these examples do not measure any listed claim version; the summary findings about alignment are recorded in R1 and R2.

untested.parts: All parts: there is no audit of neuron poles, and the model is Llama-3.2-1B, not Qwen3-32B.
All parts: one 1B dense model, and no job-share measurement.
All parts: no vision neurons and no superposition analysis.
All parts: no comparison of architectures or tools.
All parts: explanations are not tested on firing contexts.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal exploratory blog post that reports no quantitative shares. The 20 example neurons (e.g. neuron 6 'coming', neuron 14 'det') are illustrative only and are correctly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not audit neuron poles for one or two jobs or for unexplained share.
It examines Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct only, and does not assess job counts across models, architectures, or scales.
It does not analyze InceptionV1 examples, pose detection, recursive generalization, or superposition.
It does not compare architectures, regularization, interpretability tools, or interpretable-neuron shares.
It does not construct attribution graphs or assess whether neurons suffice as circuit units.
It does not test explanations against activations or firing contexts not used to write them.
It does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed the maximum absolute dot product between each layer-13 MLP output weight vector and vocabulary unembedding vectors.

conditions.value: maximum absolute dot product with a vocabulary-token embedding

rows.measure: Distribution of maximum absolute dot products across layer-13 neurons
rows.value: The distribution is non-symmetric, with a long tail of neurons close to vocabulary tokens; the post describes a significant number of aligned neurons.
rows.locator: Quantifying vocabulary alignment; Extending to other layers
rows.note: The post describes the distribution but gives no numerical summary of it in the text. This measures vocabulary alignment, not whether neurons have one main job.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. Vocabulary alignment of output weights is a different construct from neuron job counts. The distribution is shown only in plots, with no numbers in the text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared vocabulary-alignment distributions across MLP layers.

conditions.value: maximum absolute dot product with a vocabulary-token embedding

rows.value: The post states that the majority of neurons with stronger vocabulary alignment are in later blocks.
rows.note: No layer-specific numerical values are stated in the text. This result concerns vocabulary alignment rather than neuron job counts.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The layer-wise pattern is stated only qualitatively, and it concerns alignment, not interpretability share.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
